name: The Forgotten Pools
summary: At the Forgotten Pools, life surges through the dry Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids sense unseen forces beneath the earth.

sections.title: Stirrings in the Savannah
sections.body: The Barrens once flourished as fertile land before ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent. The region became sun-baked scrubland, but lush oases have recently begun taking root in its dry basin. Druids of the Cenarion Circle find this sudden growth unnatural. They sense powers beneath the earth pressing upward, stirring vegetation and wildlife into life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

sections.title: The Murky Depths
sections.body: Tonga Runetotem sends you to the Forgotten Pools, just northwest of the Crossroads, to learn more about the new growth. Beneath the water, a fissure in the earth vents strange, bubbling gases into the pool. Tonga cannot yet say what this means, but the fissure gives him a tangible clue as the Barrens changes around you.

faq.answer: Tonga Runetotem is a tauren druid of the Cenarion Circle stationed at the Crossroads. He studies the strange changes in the Barrens and seeks the reason oases are appearing across its dry plains.

faq.q: Why is the Cenarion Circle investigating the Forgotten Pools?
aliases: what is wrong with the pools
faq.answer: The Cenarion Circle investigates because its druids sense concentrated energy forcing life to the surface. They want to find the power feeding the new oases before it grows out of control.

faq.q: What is found at the bottom of the Forgotten Pools?
faq.answer: An underwater fissure vents bubbling gases into the pool. Tonga thinks it may reveal the force rising to the surface, though he cannot yet be sure.

faq.q: Where are the Forgotten Pools located?
faq.answer: The Forgotten Pools lie northwest of the Crossroads in the central Barrens. Palms and water mark the oasis amid the dry land.

faq.q: Was the Barrens always a desert?
faq.answer: No. Druidic lore says the Barrens was once lush and full of life. Ancient wars and cataclysms scorched the land, leaving the arid savannah seen today.

faq.q: What comes after investigating the Forgotten Pools?
aliases: what to do after forgotten pools
faq.answer: Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast to inspect another Barrens oasis, the Stagnant Oasis.

angles.text: As a druid, you encounter the Cenarion Circle's watch over the strange forces changing the Barrens' natural growth.
As a tauren, you know the Barrens matters to the nomadic tribes of the Earth Mother. Understanding and preserving its water sources matters to tauren travelers.
As a member of the Horde, you have reason to safeguard the water near the Crossroads, a junction between Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale.
